svg.title: Comparing a heat-included lease to a cheaper plus-hydro Canadian listing
svg.desc: Labelled winter sketch: a $2,400 heat-included unit versus a $2,150 plus-hydro electric-baseboard unit. If winter hydro runs $280 a month, the cheaper sticker is $30 more all-in. Forced-air gas and Hydro-Québec files look different. Submetered houses can hide a split-bill.
svg.text: Sticker rent lies when the heat is electric
Labelled winter month - not a utility quote. Housing lease comparison, not an OEB / Hydro-Quebec plan chooser. 20 Sep 2026.
Gap vanishes on a cold month.
Forced-air gas often wins the winter; Hydro-Québec kWh is usually cheaper than Ontario; a Winnipeg or Calgary file is another climate. Get last-winter bills or a cap in writing.
Red flags: house hydro split "however we feel," no meter, heat-included that is actually space heaters, landlord raising "utility share" off-lease.
Educational worksheet. Plan choice and time-of-use live under Utilities. BC/ON included-rent rules still cap how "heat" can be repriced as rent.
